subject: Different MCMC Behavior for "same" distribution written differently

messages.author: d128bd7b4bae8e43
messages.subject: Different MCMC Behavior for "same" distribution written differently
parts:
Hi all,

I'm working on CMR with a latent multinomial model dealing with misidentifications where latent histories are filled with 0 (non captured), 1 (captured and correcly identified) and 2 (captured and misidentified) and the vector x (that counts the number of times each latent history has been seen) follow a multinomial.
The parameters are the capture probability "p" and the identification probability "a".

I first wrote the wodel as folowing :

  # priors
  for(t in 1:S){
    p[t] ~ dbeta(1.0, 1.0)
  }
  a ~ dbeta(1.0, 1.0)
  N ~ dunif(0, 1e6)
 
  # Likelihood
  x[1:nb_hlatent] ~ dmulti(p_hist[1:nb_hlatent], size = N)
  for (i in 1:nb_hlatent){
    p_hist[i] <- proba_latent_x(latentError[i, 1:S], p[1:S], a, S)
  }

where S is the number of sampling occasion, latentError[,] a matrix containing the 3^S latent histories and proba_latent_x a nimble function defined by:

function(histo = double(1), p = double(1), a = double(0), S = double(0){
  p_histo <- 1
  for(i in 1:S){     
    if (histo[i] == 0)
        p_histo <- p_histo * (1-p[i])
      else if (histo[i] == 1)
        p_histo <- p_histo * p[i] * a
      else
        p_histo <- p_histo * p[i] * (1-a)
    }
}

Later I changed the likelihhod formulation with a specific distribution:

x[1:nb_hlatent] ~ dLMulti(capture = p[1:S], identification = a,
                            latentError = latentError[1:nb_hlatent, 1:S], nb_hlatent = nb_hlatent, S = S)

The distribution dLMulti is the following:

logProbData <- lfactorial(sum(x[1:nb_hlatent]))
    
    for(i in 1:nb_hlatent){
      logProbData <- logProbData - lfactorial(x[i])
      probHist <- 1
      for(t in 1:S){
        if(latentError[i, t] == 0)
          probHist <- probHist * (1-capture[t])
        else if(latentError[i, t] == 1)
          probHist <- probHist * capture[t] * identification
        else if(latentError[i, t] == 2)
          probHist <- probHist * capture[t] * (1-identification)
      }
      logProbData <- logProbData + x[i] * log(probHist)
    }

My problem is that even though I feel both these codes should give exacly the same results they don't.
With perfectly identical configuration of the MCMC the likelihhod implementation changes the result so that the second one converge toward the "real" posterior I'm expecting while the first gives something really far (with a = 1 as if no mistakes in identifications were made)...

Any idea why it's like this ?

Thank's already,

Best regards,
Rémi

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Different MCMC Behavior for "same" distribution written differently
parts:
Hi Rémi,

I'm not seeing anything obvious here, except to point out that Nimble's dmulti normalizes the probabilities to sum to 1 if they do not. So if it's possible that sum(p_hist[1:nb_hlatent]) is not 1, that could explain getting different results since dLmulti does not normalize. 

My suggestion would be to compare the result of dmulti() + proba_latent_x() with the result  of dLMulti() for the same input values of {latentError, p, a} and make sure they give the same likelihoods for a few different cases {latentError, p, a}.

Let us know how it goes or if you have more questions.

-Chris

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: Different MCMC Behavior for "same" distribution written differently
parts:
Hi Rémi,

Ok, if you are getting the same likelihoods, and if the MCMC configurations are exactly the same and if the initial values are the same, and the random seed is set to be the same at the start of each of the two MCMCs, I would definitely expect the MCMC samples to be the same. A few thoughts:

1) Check carefully that the initial values are the same. 

2) I'm guessing that the two MCMCs show different sampled values within the first few iterations. If so, you could use the debugging strategy I suggested in a recent post on this list (titled "RW_llFunction_block").
Namely set up debugging on one or more of the samplers, via:

debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[1]]$run)
debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[2]]$run)
etc.

Then do mcmc$run(10) to start an MCMC going. This will put you into R's debugger in the actual code where the sampling is occurring for a given node. 

Do this in separate R sessions for your two different model specifications and see if you can narrow down exactly where the two MCMCs start to give different results. 

(If it takes a number of iterations for the two MCMCs to show different values, then debugging the uncompiled MCMC may be tedious because it may take a while for the uncompiled MCMC to get to the point where the two sets of samples start to diverge...)

-Chris

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Different MCMC Behavior for "same" distribution written differently
parts:
Hi Remí,

Here are a few more comments.

I see the second version explicitly checks for the 2, while the first version assumes that all elements not 0 or 1 must be 2.  I assume they are consistent.  Just pointing out this minor discrepancy in the code.

You haven't shown the full nimbleFunction code for dLMulti.  There are a couple of possible pitfalls to be sure to avoid.  One is that even though some of the inputs will in fact be integers, they should be treated as doubles.  E.g. you should have "x = double(1)", not "x = integer(1)", as an argument.  Another is that you should be sure you are respecting the (required) log argument and returning the logProbData value when log=1 (TRUE), i.e. not accidentally returning exp(logProbData).

Chris suggested a debugging strategy involving stepping through samplers.  Here is a suggestion for debugging focused on the model itself.  You can do:

model <- nimbleModel(<your inputs>)
model$calculate()
model$p <- some_test_values_for_p
<set other values of the model>
model$calculate()
model$logProb_X[1] # equivalently model$getLogProb("X")

and then to track down any strange behavior you can do 
debug(dLMulti)
model$calculate()
to step through exactly what the inputs and calculations of dLMulti are.

You could make two models (your first and second versions) at the same time and check each step of calculation piece by piece using the two.

I hope it helps.  Let us know how it goes.
-Perry

Hi,

Thank's a lot for how to debug the execution it really helped. Here's the answer to my problem (and a small question at the end):
So just like I thought for fixed values of p, a and x both  "dmulti() + proba_latent_x()" and "dLMulti()" calculate the same thing.
The difference in results arise at the first iteration (this also solves my other post about the initialization).
The "dmulti() + proba_latent_x()" doesn't work because at the begginning I update the value of a and p (with a Gibbs personnal sampler so the initialization doesn't matter) BUT when I sample x_prop and calculate the likelihood, the model didn't update the value of p_hist =  proba_latent_x(p,a) in the model accordingly to the new values of p and a...

When is the p_hist value of the model updated ? It just depends on "a" and "p" so I imagined it would automaticaly update if any of them changed but is it even automatically updated or if one never specify it it won't get updated ?

Rémi

You haven't shown the full nimbleFunction code for dLMulti.  There are a couple of possible pitfalls to be sure to avoid.  One is that even though some of the inputs will in fact be integers, they should be treated as doubles.  E.g. you should have "x = double(1)", not "x = integer(1)", as an argument.  Another is that you should be sure you are respecting the (required) log argument and returning the logProbData value when log=1 (TRUE), i.e. not accidentally returning exp(logProbData).

Chris suggested a debugging strategy involving stepping through samplers.  Here is a suggestion for debugging focused on the model itself.  You can do:

model <- nimbleModel(<your inputs>)
model$calculate()
model$p <- some_test_values_for_p
<set other values of the model>
model$calculate()
model$logProb_X[1] # equivalently model$getLogProb("X")

and then to track down any strange behavior you can do 
debug(dLMulti)
model$calculate()
to step through exactly what the inputs and calculations of dLMulti are.

I hope it helps.  Let us know how it goes.

On Tue, Jun 22, 2021 at 12:26 PM Chris Paciorek <christophe...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hi Rémi,

Ok, if you are getting the same likelihoods, and if the MCMC configurations are exactly the same and if the initial values are the same, and the random seed is set to be the same at the start of each of the two MCMCs, I would definitely expect the MCMC samples to be the same. A few thoughts:

1) Check carefully that the initial values are the same. 

2) I'm guessing that the two MCMCs show different sampled values within the first few iterations. If so, you could use the debugging strategy I suggested in a recent post on this list (titled "RW_llFunction_block").
Namely set up debugging on one or more of the samplers, via:

debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[1]]$run)
debug(mcmc$samplerFunctions[[2]]$run)
etc.

Then do mcmc$run(10) to start an MCMC going. This will put you into R's debugger in the actual code where the sampling is occurring for a given node. 

Do this in separate R sessions for your two different model specifications and see if you can narrow down exactly where the two MCMCs start to give different results. 

(If it takes a number of iterations for the two MCMCs to show different values, then debugging the uncompiled MCMC may be tedious because it may take a while for the uncompiled MCMC to get to the point where the two sets of samples start to diverge...)

-Chris

On Mon, Jun 21, 2021 at 2:23 AM Rémi <fra...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi all,

I'm working on CMR with a latent multinomial model dealing with misidentifications where latent histories are filled with 0 (non captured), 1 (captured and correcly identified) and 2 (captured and misidentified) and the vector x (that counts the number of times each latent history has been seen) follow a multinomial.
The parameters are the capture probability "p" and the identification probability "a".

I first wrote the wodel as folowing :

  # priors
  for(t in 1:S){
    p[t] ~ dbeta(1.0, 1.0)
  }
  a ~ dbeta(1.0, 1.0)
  N ~ dunif(0, 1e6)
 
  # Likelihood
  x[1:nb_hlatent] ~ dmulti(p_hist[1:nb_hlatent], size = N)
  for (i in 1:nb_hlatent){
    p_hist[i] <- proba_latent_x(latentError[i, 1:S], p[1:S], a, S)
  }

where S is the number of sampling occasion, latentError[,] a matrix containing the 3^S latent histories and proba_latent_x a nimble function defined by:

function(histo = double(1), p = double(1), a = double(0), S = double(0){
  p_histo <- 1
  for(i in 1:S){     
    if (histo[i] == 0)
        p_histo <- p_histo * (1-p[i])
      else if (histo[i] == 1)
        p_histo <- p_histo * p[i] * a
      else
        p_histo <- p_histo * p[i] * (1-a)
    }
}

Later I changed the likelihhod formulation with a specific distribution:

x[1:nb_hlatent] ~ dLMulti(capture = p[1:S], identification = a,
                            latentError = latentError[1:nb_hlatent, 1:S], nb_hlatent = nb_hlatent, S = S)

The distribution dLMulti is the following:

logProbData <- lfactorial(sum(x[1:nb_hlatent]))
    
    for(i in 1:nb_hlatent){
      logProbData <- logProbData - lfactorial(x[i])
      probHist <- 1
      for(t in 1:S){
        if(latentError[i, t] == 0)
          probHist <- probHist * (1-capture[t])
        else if(latentError[i, t] == 1)
          probHist <- probHist * capture[t] * identification
        else if(latentError[i, t] == 2)
          probHist <- probHist * capture[t] * (1-identification)
      }
      logProbData <- logProbData + x[i] * log(probHist)
    }

My problem is that even though I feel both these codes should give exacly the same results they don't.
With perfectly identical configuration of the MCMC the likelihhod implementation changes the result so that the second one converge toward the "real" posterior I'm expecting while the first gives something really far (with a = 1 as if no mistakes in identifications were made)...

Any idea why it's like this ?

Thank's already,

Best regards,
Rémi

parts:
Hi Rémi,

That's great news that you've found the source of the problem and made use of some debugging steps.

Let me try to explain more about nimble's model-generic programming concepts.  It is tempting to think that the model is designed to be clever for you, but it isn't.  When we first designed the system, we were repeatedly tempted to make it automatically clever in some way.  But the system is designed for programming potentially arbitrary algorithms, and what seems clever for one algorithm can be wasteful for another.  In your example, perhaps you are going to calculate only the logProb of the priors for a and p and then replace them with new values.  In that case it would be wasteful to automatically calculate something that depends on them.  Or if you do need the dependency calculated, should it be calculated when a is changed and then again when p is changed, in which case the first calculation would be wasteful?  For these kinds of reasons, an important design principle of nimble is that models are not smart.  Instead a programmer needs to understand and use models correctly.  The model is a machine and the programmer has fairly complete control over the machine and is responsible for telling it what to calculate.  I hope that helps explain why it was not as clever as you imagined it might be.  Portions of our User Manual cover how to use models and also the requirements of writing your own samplers to comply with the MCMC system.  One requirement for a sampler to be valid in the MCMC system is that it must always leave both the model and the saved model states (mvStates) up to date, i.e. with dependencies calculated, which you as the programmer need to ensure.  We welcome suggestions on improving the User Manual or other sources of documentation (R help pages, web site examples).

Thanks and I hope you've got what you need to move ahead!

-Perry

When is the p_hist value of the model updated ? It just depends on "a" and "p" so I imagined it would automaticaly update if any of them changed but is it even automatically updated or if one never specify it it won't get updated ?
